sentences.text: The present transfer application has been preferred by the applicant-wife under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, seeking transfer of Case No. 952/2022, filed by the respondent-husband under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, and presently pending before the learned Family Court No.1, Jodhpur, to the learned Family Court, Phalodi, District Jodhpur.

2. Perusal of the transfer application reveals that the applicant is already prosecuting a matrimonial case under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, registered as Case No. 39/2021 (Smt. Durga Kanwar v. Sujan Singh), before the Family Court, Phalodi, seeking dissolution of marriage.

pending before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Phalodi, pursuant to a charge-sheet filed against the respondent and his relatives.
Cognizance was taken on 07.01.2020.
3. It has been further asserted that she is without independent income and is solely responsible for the care of two minor children and an aged father.
It is her case that compelling her to travel from Phalodi to Jodhpur to contest proceedings would inflict financial, mental, and physical hardship.

4. Upon consideration of the record, it is evident that the applicant is already engaged in both civil and criminal litigation against the respondent at Phalodi.
The respondent is required to appear before the Courts at Phalodi in connection with the said proceedings.
No substantial prejudice would be caused to him by transferring the present case to Phalodi.
5. It is a well-settled principle of law that in matrimonial matters, the convenience of the wife is to be given predominant consideration.

In Sumita Singh v. Kumar Sanjay, (2001) 10 SCC 41, and Rajani Kishor Pardeshi v. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) 12 SCC 237, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has categorically held that the wife should not be compelled to travel long distances for litigation.

Accordingly, the transfer application is allowed and it is ordered that the Case No. 952/2022, filed by the respondent under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, and presently pending before the learned Family Court No.1, Jodhpur, shall stand transferred to the learned Family Court,
Phalodi, District Jodhpur, for trial and disposal in accordance with law.

The learned Family Court,
Jodhpur, is directed to transmit the entire record of the case to the transferee Court at Phalodi without delay.

8. Upon transfer, both matters pending between the parties under the Hindu Marriage Act shall be heard and disposed of by the learned Family Court, Phalodi, expeditiously and preferably in accordance with the timeline prescribed under law.
9. All pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
